# T2.05d: observe a working NVENC client (nullmoth's library), replay its setup

Approved by the user on 2026-10-18 (option B): observe nullmoth's closed `libnvenc_h264.dylib` at its RM/IOKit
boundary and capture what it pushes to the GPU. No disassembly, no patching of the library.

## Tools

- **`trace/nvtrace.c`** → `nvtrace.dylib`, loaded with `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`. It interposes `IOServiceOpen`,
  `IOConnectCallMethod`/`ScalarMethod`/`StructMethod` and `IOConnectMapMemory64`, and logs every RM escape with
  its parameters and calling image: allocations (memory type/flags/attr/attr2/size, channel params), controls,
  `MAP_MEMORY_DMA` flags and GPU addresses, CPU mappings. For channels on an NVENC engine it follows the GPFIFO
  from a polling thread, decodes each pushed segment (methods per subchannel), and at every NVENC `EXECUTE` logs the
  method state, the memory object behind every address, the picture setup (32 KB) and the RC buffers.
  `NVTRACE_DIR=<dir>` also writes each buffer raw (`exec<N>-<method>.bin`).
- **`tools/vtrandom.m`**: encodes one random NV12 frame through VideoToolbox's hardware encoder and writes the source.
  The plugin's NVENC knob goes by process name, so run it as `vttest` (copy it to `/tmp/vtr/vttest`).
- **`scripts/trace2blob.py`** pulls a dump out of a log into a binary file.
- Captures are in `docs/traces/` (`vttest-256x128-3f.log`, picture setups of frames 1-3).

## What the working client does differently

Run: `vttest hw avc1 256 128 3` (51.2 dB). The library opens its own RM client, allocates everything itself (sysmem
`NV01_MEMORY_SYSTEM` attr 0x2a800000 attr2 0x9, vidmem `NV01_MEMORY_LOCAL_USER` attr 0x10800000 attr2 0x5,
`MAP_MEMORY_DMA` flags 0x18 / 0x8), and creates a channel on NVENC0 (engineType 0x1b) with a `0xc9b7` object.

| | ours (encode1) | reference |
|---|---|---|
| magic | 0xC9B70006 (nvenc_drv.h, NV_NVENC_8_2) | **0xCFB70006** |
| SET_CONTROL_PARAMS | 0x103 (H.264, force out pic) | **0x1303** (+ SLICE_STAT_ON, GPTIMER_ON) |
| input surface | block-linear bh 1, `bl_tile_plane` | block_height 2, but a **different tile layout** (below) |
| recon surface | tiled_16x16 = 1 ("must be 1 for refpics", says the doc) | **block_height 2, tiled_16x16 = 0** |
| chroma | `CHROMA_U` = picture base + chroma offset in setup | `CHROMA_U` = `CHROMA_V` = chroma plane, offsets 0 |
| extra methods | 14 scratch buffers | `SET_IN_RCDATA` (vidmem 64 KB) and `SET_IO_RC_PROCESS` (vidmem 1 MB) only, both zero |
| controls | at 512/640/832/960 | ME 0x3000, MD 0x3c00, quant 0x4400, slice 0x5000, WP 0x7000 |
| SPS/PPS fields | poc type 0, 1 ref | poc type 2, log2_max_frame_num-4 = 4, 3 L0 refs |
| field offsets | 0 | luma_bot 0x40, chroma_bot 0x20 (in 256 B) even for frames |
| history | 64 KB, size field ours | 4 MB buffer, `hist_buf_size` 0x1800 |

## Replay

`encode1` got `NVENC_REPLAY=<blob>`: the captured 32 KB setup replaces ours, with the reference method set and our own
buffers (the setup holds only offsets, no GPU addresses). Result: **the engine encodes** (2.3 ms, one IDR slice, 128
intra MBs) and Apple's decoder accepts it with SPS/PPS written from the setup's fields. `h264hdr` now supports POC
type 2 and a PPS L0 ref count. But PSNR was 10 dB: our input tiling was wrong.

## The input layout, measured

With `vtrandom` under `nvtrace` (random 256x128 frame), every 8-byte chunk of the source was found exactly once in
the input surface the library hands the engine (`exec1-734.bin`, after the plugin's classic-layout patch). The mapping
for luma and chroma alike:

    off = (y/16)*pitch*16 + (x/64)*1024
        + (x%16) + 16*(y%4) + 64*((x/16)%2) + 128*((y/4)%2) + 256*((x/32)%2) + 512*((y/8)%2)

That's 64-byte x 16-row tiles of 1 KB, row-major, with 16-byte x 4-row sub-blocks inside. It is **not** the classic
64x8 GOB that `bl_tile_plane` writes. Added as `nvenc_in_tile_plane()` in `src/blocklinear.c` (`NVENC_VAR=tileada`).

**Replay + measured layout: luma 50.38 dB, chroma 52.20 dB** (256x128, encode 0.09 ms). M2's quality goal is met
with the reference setup. Next (T2.05e): find which differences matter, so our own setup (from nvenc_drv.h) works
without a captured blob.
